title: vl04: the matrix of the adjoint is stated for 'the finite-dimensional case' without the inner product

legacy.old_text: Daher, im dem endlich-dimensionalen Fall wird die adjungierte Matrix wie folgt dargestellt
legacy.new_text: Daher wird im endlichdimensionalen Fall, mit dem Standardskalarprodukt, die adjungierte Matrix wie folgt dargestellt
legacy.applied_text: In $\mathbb{C}^n$ mit $\vb{v}\adj\vb{w}$ heißt das Kreuz: erst transponieren

legacy.old_text: Hence, in the finite-dimensional case, the adjoint matrix is represented as follows
legacy.new_text: Hence, in the finite-dimensional case with the standard inner product, the adjoint matrix is represented as follows
legacy.applied_text: In $\mathbb{C}^n$ with $\vb{v}\adj\vb{w}$ the dagger means: first transpose

reason: The adjoint operator is defined through the inner product (vl04.tex:35-37), so the conjugate transpose matrix represents it only for the standard inner product of C^n (in an orthonormal basis). For a weighted product the adjoint of a 2x2 matrix differs from the conjugate transpose (example checked in evidence/derivations/c03/check_c03.py). The old sentence also has the grammar slip 'im dem' and a comma after 'Daher'. The new text names the inner product and says that for another one the adjoint is in general not the conjugate transpose matrix.
